questiontext.text: Which access specifier is normally used to hide a class's internal data members?

answer.text: private

feedback.text: Correct — private members are inaccessible outside the class.

answer.text: public

feedback.text: No — public members are exposed to all callers.

answer.text: extern

feedback.text: No — extern is about linkage, not access control.

answer.text: virtual

feedback.text: No — virtual concerns dispatch, not data hiding.

generalfeedback.text: Marking data members private hides internal state; access flows through the public interface.

questiontext.text: How does a well-encapsulated class typically expose controlled access to its private data?

answer.text: Through public getter/setter methods (a controlled interface)

feedback.text: Correct — accessors mediate reads and writes.

answer.text: By making every data member public

feedback.text: No — that removes the control entirely.

answer.text: By deleting all member functions

feedback.text: No — then there would be no interface at all.

answer.text: By declaring the whole class static

feedback.text: No — static does not provide controlled access.

generalfeedback.text: Public getters/setters give a controlled interface so the class can validate and protect its state.

questiontext.text: What is a key benefit of hiding internal state behind a public interface?

answer.text: It protects the class invariants and lets the implementation change freely

feedback.text: Correct — callers depend on the interface, not the internals.

answer.text: It guarantees the program runs faster at run time

feedback.text: No — encapsulation is about maintainability, not raw speed.

answer.text: It removes the need for any public methods

feedback.text: No — the public interface is what callers use.

answer.text: It makes all members accessible from anywhere

feedback.text: No — that is the opposite of hiding state.

generalfeedback.text: Hiding state protects invariants and decouples callers from the implementation, which can then evolve safely.
